scope: Focused primary-source review, not a systematic review

literature.title: Inferring Regulatory Networks from Expression Data Using Tree-Based Methods
literature.read_extent: Primary publisher abstract and method/introduction excerpts.
claims: GENIE3 decomposes GRN inference into target-wise regression and combines tree-ensemble feature importance into regulatory-edge rankings.
literature.relevance: Established expression-based inference family; cite as context, not a completed GCEV comparator.
literature.caution: Predictive feature importance does not establish direct causality.

literature.title: GRNBoost2 and Arboreto: efficient and scalable inference of gene regulatory networks
literature.read_extent: Publisher abstract and gradient-boosting/scalability method excerpts; PubMed metadata.
claims: GRNBoost2 uses gradient boosting for the target-wise regression strategy; Arboreto provides scalable parallel execution.
literature.relevance: Scalable baseline family for a later standard-method comparison.
literature.caution: GCEV's small Ridge-based experiments are not a benchmark against GRNBoost2.

literature.title: Gene Regulatory Network Inference from Single-Cell Data Using Multivariate Information Measures
literature.read_extent: PMC abstract and multivariate-information method excerpts; PubMed metadata.
claims: PIDC uses partial information decomposition across gene triplets and local network context to infer putative relationships from single-cell expression.
literature.relevance: Shows that established inference extends beyond pairwise correlation.
literature.caution: Information-theoretic association is not equivalent to a validated directed regulatory edge.

literature.title: SCENIC: single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering
literature.read_extent: Publisher/PubMed abstract and PMC pipeline-method excerpts.
claims: SCENIC combines expression-derived coexpression modules, cis-regulatory motif analysis and cell-level regulon activity to characterize cell states.
literature.relevance: Motif-supported GRN construction is established prior art.
literature.caution: The GCEV novelty claim cannot be the mere addition of motif information.

literature.title: High-performance single-cell gene regulatory network inference at scale: the Inferelator 3.0
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and regularized-regression/prior-network method excerpts.
claims: Inferelator 3.0 combines expression with prior regulatory connections using regularized regression, supports motif/chromatin-derived priors, and estimates context-specific and shared networks.
literature.relevance: Direct prior-informed regression comparator; prior use and context specificity are not new in GCEV.
literature.caution: Do not attribute every historical Inferelator feature to the exact implementation used in this paper.

literature.title: Passing messages between biological networks to refine predicted interactions
literature.read_extent: Primary PubMed abstract and method/figure-description excerpts linked to PMC3669401.
claims: PANDA iteratively reconciles motif-derived TF–gene, protein-interaction and coexpression networks by message passing.
literature.relevance: Network-structured heterogeneous evidence integration predates GCEV.
literature.caution: Graph context alone is not a defensible novelty claim.

literature.title: SCENIC+: single-cell multiomic inference of enhancers and gene regulatory networks
literature.read_extent: Publisher abstract, methods and comparison excerpts.
claims: SCENIC+ infers enhancer-centered regulatory networks by integrating accessibility, expression and motif evidence into TF–region and region–gene relationships.
literature.relevance: Modern multiomic comparator and motivation for separating the information carried by different sources.
literature.caution: GCEV's separate RNA and DNase sources do not constitute paired single-cell multiome data.

literature.title: Dissecting cell identity via network inference and in silico gene perturbation
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and base-GRN, accessibility and motif-ablation method excerpts.
claims: CellOracle constructs motif/accessibility-informed base networks, estimates context-specific expression relationships and models in silico TF perturbations.
The paper tests impaired base networks, including scrambled motifs and no base network.
literature.relevance: Source ablations and motif-supported priors are established practices.
literature.caution: In silico perturbations are model predictions, distinct from experimental interventions; do not call GCEV the first source-ablation study.

literature.title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell multiome data using atlas-scale external data
literature.read_extent: Publisher abstract and lifelong-learning/model-method excerpts.
claims: LINGER combines atlas-scale external data, single-cell multiome measurements and motif information through lifelong neural-network learning.
literature.relevance: External priors and adaptive representation learning have substantial prior art.
literature.caution: No matched quantitative comparison with this large-data model has been performed in GCEV.

literature.title: Optimizing data integration improves gene regulatory network inference in Arabidopsis thaliana
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and extensive prior-integration-strength optimization methods.
claims: DIOgene optimizes gene-specific integration strength for biological priors using expression-prediction error, measures of effective integration and a simulated null.
The approach addresses tuning when available gold standards are incomplete or related to the prior.
literature.relevance: Closest precedent for adapting prior weight from predictive usefulness.
literature.caution: Do not claim first adaptive prior integration, first gene-specific prior weighting, or first predictive-fit-based integration.

literature.title: Genes2Reg: Constructing a biologically-faithful gene coupling prior via deep adaptive fusion of heterogeneous knowledge sources
literature.publication_status: Peer-reviewed accepted early version, published 2026-10-17; no volume/article number verified.
literature.read_extent: Publisher abstract, author metadata and adaptive-fusion description.
claims: Genes2Reg uses heterogeneous graph attention to fuse heterogeneous biological knowledge into a symmetric gene-coupling prior for downstream use.
Its motivation and formulation explicitly involve adaptive weighting of knowledge sources.
literature.relevance: Closest precedent for generic adaptive reliability-aware evidence fusion.
literature.caution: The narrower proposed GCEV distinction is conditional marginal utility for candidate graph actions, not adaptive fusion itself. Do not invent an article number.

literature.title: Benchmarking algorithms for gene regulatory network inference from single-cell transcriptomic data
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and evaluation/results excerpts.
claims: BEELINE compares single-cell GRN methods across synthetic, Boolean-model and experimental data with edge-recovery metrics.
Method performance depends on the data and reference-network setting.
literature.relevance: Standard benchmark framework for future comparisons.
literature.caution: A predictive NMSE improvement is not interchangeable with improved edge recovery.

literature.title: A large-scale benchmark for network inference from single-cell perturbation data
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and extensive interventional-evaluation methods/results.
claims: CausalBench evaluates methods on large K562 and RPE1 perturbation datasets using complementary biological and intervention-distribution assessments.
It explicitly works under incomplete knowledge of the true causal network.
literature.relevance: Strong motivation for independent intervention-based evaluation and explicit estimands.
literature.caution: Knockdown-associated response and direct TF binding measure different relationships; neither alone recovers a complete causal graph.

literature.title: BEAR-GRN: Systematic assessment of single-cell multi-omics-based gene regulatory network inference methods
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and detailed ground-truth, modality-perturbation and metric-method excerpts; publisher supplement author list.
claims: BEAR-GRN evaluates single-cell multiomic methods across multiple reference definitions and investigates modality contribution with controlled perturbations.
Many evaluated methods are predominantly RNA-driven, with limited independent accessibility contribution under its benchmarks.
literature.relevance: Direct prior art for diagnosing weak modality use; essential current comparison.
literature.caution: Do not generalize GCEV's additive target-constant invariance into a claim that accessibility has no biological value. Benchmark rankings depend on reference and negative-sampling conventions.

literature.title: Dissecting and improving gene regulatory network inference using single-cell transcriptome data
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and mechanistic-model introduction/results excerpts.
claims: Mechanistic analysis shows that mature mRNA can be an imperfect proxy for upstream regulatory activity; intronic information can improve some inference settings.
literature.relevance: Explains why expression prediction and regulatory mechanism must remain separate claims.
literature.caution: This paper does not validate the distributional suitability of the particular GCEV expression files.

literature.title: Topological benchmarking of algorithms to infer gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq data
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and topological-evaluation methods; PubMed metadata.
claims: STREAMLINE evaluates inferred-network topology and hub recovery, complementing edge-wise scoring.
literature.relevance: Encourages reporting graph structure as a separate endpoint.
literature.caution: Describing graph topology without a suitable reference does not establish topological accuracy.

literature.title: JASPAR 2026: expansion of transcription factor binding profiles and integration of deep learning models
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and collection-description excerpts; PubMed full author/issue metadata.
claims: JASPAR 2026 expands curated TF binding profiles and adds a separate deep-learning-model collection.
literature.relevance: Correct resource release for the frozen motif source.
literature.caution: GCEV used selected CORE motif matrices; it did not use the new deep learning models. Resource-level citation does not prove independence of a particular motif's experimental derivation.

literature.title: Expanded encyclopaedias of DNA elements in the human and mouse genomes
literature.read_extent: Primary publisher abstract and assay/resource-method excerpts; contributor-institution publication metadata. Opened PubMed author roster and abstract.
claims: ENCODE phase III expanded transcript, chromatin and TF-occupancy resources across biological contexts and provides data through its portal.
literature.relevance: Resource provenance for accessibility, binding and perturbation metadata.
literature.caution: Different assays represent different biological measurements. Matching the K562 label does not by itself establish matched samples or independent experiments.
literature.authors_note: Full named-author roster verified against the opened PubMed article record; consortium collaborators are not expanded.

literature.title: GENCODE reference annotation for the human and mouse genomes
literature.read_extent: Primary resource abstract and official GENCODE publication list.
claims: GENCODE combines manual annotation, computational pipelines and supporting evidence to provide reference human and mouse gene annotations.
literature.relevance: General annotation citation for the frozen GENCODE v29-derived promoters.
literature.caution: The paper does not establish the exact GCEV promoter-window convention; cite the actual v29 file and pipeline manifest separately.
literature.authors_note: Exact surname/initial roster transcribed from the official GENCODE publication list.

literature.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
literature.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological)
literature.read_extent: Primary publisher summary and bibliographic record.
claims: The paper defines false-discovery-rate control and establishes the BH step-up procedure under the conditions studied.
literature.relevance: Cite for the reported motif multiple-testing adjustment.
literature.caution: A result of zero BH discoveries is not proof of no biological signal; validity depends on the p-values and dependence assumptions. Do not claim unconditional FDR control.

literature.title: Bias in error estimation when using cross-validation for model selection
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and nested-CV conclusion; publisher PDF metadata.
claims: Using the same cross-validation results for model selection and error estimation can yield optimistic estimates; nested evaluation reduced that bias in the studied simulations.
literature.relevance: Motivates separation of model/weight selection from final held-out performance.
literature.caution: Target-group out-of-fold nuisance estimation is not automatically equivalent to complete nested model selection or causal cross-fitting.

literature.title: Wisdom of crowds for robust gene network inference
literature.read_extent: Primary abstract and DREAM challenge-design/result excerpts; PubMed author list.
claims: DREAM5 found context-dependent performance among network-inference methods and robust results from community combinations in the evaluated settings.
literature.relevance: Classical evidence for complementary inference biases and consensus integration.
literature.caution: Method ensembles differ from evidence-source fusion; the paper is not evidence that every multi-source scheme improves inference.

literature.title: GLM-Prior: a genomic language model for transferable sequence-derived priors in gene regulatory network inference
literature.publication_status: Published 2026-09-14; full volume/article metadata verified in PubMed. Publisher search text still displays an early-version notice.
literature.read_extent: Primary publisher abstract and extensive PMC model, training, prior-conditioning and evaluation-method excerpts.
claims: GLM-Prior fine-tunes a genomic language model to construct TF–gene priors, then conditions expression-based GRN inference on those priors.
Across its evaluated contexts, prior quality strongly influences downstream benchmark performance.
literature.relevance: Current evidence for evaluating prior construction separately from the downstream inference algorithm.
literature.caution: Reference-database classification and unlabeled-negative conventions are not exhaustive causal truth; do not transfer the paper's performance numbers to GCEV.
